newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti unions urge support for company.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti unions urge support for company.

text.p: Unions at Olivetti say they support the company's search for international partners and want government initiatives to help Italy's information technology sector, but are against the dismemberment of the ailing group.
Leaders of Italy's three main engineering unions were putting forward their demands for the recovery of Olivetti to a lower house parliamentary commission.
The leader of the unions Fiom, Fim and Uilm say they do not want economic help from the state, but a industrial policy to defend Italy's position in the information technology sector.
"Olivetti is the tenth largest information technology group in the world and carries an important role for Italy's international standing in the sector," said Gianni Italia of Fim.

Union leaders urged the government to act to increase public demand in the sector and said it was necessary for the company to seek out an international partner, while maintaining the group's own identity.

Claudio Sabattini of Fiom said that Olivetti has been reduced to the bone so that any further rationalisation could lead to a worsening of the situation. This was in relation to talk that Olivetti will sell-off its personal computer company.
"We are against a break-up of the group because it is necessary to have a strong company to be able to form international alliances," Sabattini said.
"The unions can not accept a break-up of the group" and in that case "it would start a very serious conflict," he said.
